output.summary: The deterministic LT Verdict is PASS with run validity VALID and analysis coverage COMPLETE; this advice does not change that verdict. The capacity analysis verified a LOWER_BOUND of 297 concurrent users on the load axis "users" (achieved statistic p05_10s), with all three steps passing the latency policy (response_time_p95_ms observed 140 vs threshold 250 in every stage) and zero errors (error_count 0, error_rate_ratio 0/3601, sample_count 3601). The recorded bound is 297 rather than the nominal 300 because the achieved statistic is the 5th percentile of 10-second active-user cells. No capacity knee is reported (knee_reason KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED) and upper_exclusive is null, so the actual ceiling is unknown. All window policy summaries carry resource_verdict NO_POLICY; the only resource policy evaluated is the load-generator CPU guard (threshold 0.85, observed max 0.45), so server-side resource headroom was not measured. Generator CPU statistics are identical across all three stages despite load rising 100→200→300 users. The throughput_rps ratio 3601000/900500 corresponds to roughly 4 requests/s over 3601 samples. Clock alignment is not_verified_by_core, so no temporal or causal ordering is supported. Key follow-ups: instrument the server side, enable or perform knee detection, verify clocks, and confirm that 300 active users generate the intended request rate.

hypotheses.observation: All three window policy summaries report resource_verdict NO_POLICY (analysis-result.json#/evidence/13, /15, /17), and the only resource policy evaluations present are generator-cpu-guard checks (threshold 0.85, status PASS) against a generator CPU series that stays ~0.41-0.45 across stages 1-3 (analysis-result.json#/evidence/4, /6, /8, /9, /10, /11).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The monitored resource dimension is the load generator's CPU, not the system under test. Flat generator CPU does not indicate server headroom; server-side CPU, memory, or queue saturation could exist without being measured, so capacity (297 users) is asserted only against latency and generator CPU, not SUT resources.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Add SUT-side resource metrics and policy checks (CPU, memory, GC, queue depth) to future capacity runs so the PASS verdict covers the service under test rather than only the load generator.

hypotheses.observation: capacity_knee is null with knee_reason KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, upper_exclusive is null, and only lower_inclusive 297 is defined in the capacity summary (analysis-result.json#/capacity_summary and analysis-result.json#/evidence/18).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The run establishes only that at least 297 users satisfy the policies; it does not estimate the load at which capacity degrades, because no knee detector executed and no failing step was encountered.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Enable or implement a knee detector, or extend the run with additional escalating load steps until a failing step or knee is observed, so an upper_exclusive capacity ceiling can be estimated.

hypotheses.observation: With 300 users targeted in stage-3, achieved p05_10s is 297 and observed_min is 297 (analysis-result.json#/evidence/7); the overall metric summary reports sample_count 3601 and throughput_rps numerator/denominator 3601000/900500 (ratio roughly 4 rps), while p95 latency is 140 ms in each stage policy check (analysis-result.json#/evidence/0, /12, /14, /16).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The active-user count may not translate into a proportionally high request rate if the workload is pacing/think-time dominated; a modest total of 3601 samples over the run means flat p95 latency of 140 ms across steps is not strong evidence that the service was heavily saturated at 300 users.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Review the JMeter/load configuration (think times, pacing, ramp) and compute per-user request rate to confirm that 300 active users produce the intended request mix and request-per-second load.

hypotheses.observation: The verified bound is 297 (p05_10s) in every stage even though nominal targets are 100/200/300; observed_min trails target by 3 users in each stage, and stage-3 has a slightly negative slope_per_second (-0.000378) with split_half_shift 1 (analysis-result.json#/evidence/3, /5, /7, /18).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Minor dips or measurement quantization in the 10-second active-user cells lower the p05 below the nominal target, so the deterministic verified load is 297 rather than 300; this is within the 0.05 target tolerance but it is the reason the recorded bound differs from the nominal target.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the raw 10-second active-user cells, especially around stage boundaries, to confirm the 3-user shortfall is due to ramp or measurement behavior rather than a load-shaping defect.

hypotheses.observation: Generator CPU statistics (max 0.45, mean 0.43, min 0.41, sample_standard_deviation 0.01438) are identical across stage-1, stage-2, and stage-3 while active users rise 100→200→300 (analysis-result.json#/evidence/4, /6, /8).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The identical statistics across different load levels may reflect coarse metric resolution, quantized reporting, or background noise on the generator rather than true load insensitivity; equally, the generator may simply have been far below saturation in all stages.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the raw generator-cpu series (unit, resolution, and cell-to-cell variation) to determine whether the identical statistics are a measurement artifact before using them to draw conclusions.

hypotheses.observation: The run reports error_count 0 and error_rate_ratio 0/3601 with analysis coverage COMPLETE, but the only transaction-scope metric summary present is for the 'checkout' JMETER_SAMPLER (analysis-result.json#/evidence/0, /1, analysis-result.json#/analysis_coverage).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: An error-free, coverage-complete result corroborates PASS for the measured envelope; however, the absence of errors and empty findings list does not prove stability outside that envelope, and any other transactions in the scenario were not summarized.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Extend scenario coverage to additional transaction types and longer or burstier runs, and confirm 0 error counts per sampler beyond 'checkout'.

hypotheses.observation: resource_binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core for the evaluation windows (analysis-result.json#/evidence/2), while the active-users series report split_half_shift values of -1, 0, and 1 across stages (analysis-result.json#/evidence/3, /5, /7).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Without verified clock alignment between the load generator and any server-side telemetry, no lead/lag ordering or temporal causal hypothesis (e.g., load changes causing latency changes) can be inferred from these series.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock alignment/time synchronization across the load generator and server-side measurement sources before drawing any temporal or causal conclusions.

recommendations.action: Instrument the system under test with resource metrics (CPU, memory, GC, queue depth) and add resource policy checks to capacity runs.
recommendations.rationale: All window summaries carry resource_verdict NO_POLICY and the only resource guard evaluated is generator-cpu (threshold 0.85), so the PASS verdict does not reflect server-side headroom.

recommendations.action: Enable or implement a knee detector, or escalate load beyond 300 users until a failing step, so an upper capacity bound can be estimated.
recommendations.rationale: capacity_knee is null with reason KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED and upper_exclusive is null; only the lower bound (297 users) is known and the ceiling is undetermined.

recommendations.action: Verify clock alignment/time synchronization between the load generator and all server-side telemetry.
recommendations.rationale: resource_binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core, which prevents any temporal ordering or causal interpretation of the series.

recommendations.action: Validate the load scenario configuration (think times, pacing, ramp) and per-user request rate so 300 active users produce the intended request-per-second load.
recommendations.rationale: The run contains 3601 samples with a throughput_rps ratio of about 4 rps (3601000/900500); without confirming request-rate behavior, the flat 140 ms p95 across 100→200→300 users is weak evidence of saturation at 300 users.

recommendations.action: Inspect the raw 10-second active-user cells at stage boundaries and confirm the definition and behavior of the p05_10s achieved statistic.
recommendations.rationale: The verified bound is 297 in steps targeting 100/200/300, indicating a consistent 3-user shortfall between observed_min and target; understanding whether this is ramp or measurement behavior clarifies the reported capacity bound.

recommendations.action: Broaden scenario coverage to include other transactions, longer durations, and burst profiles, then re-check error counts per sampler.
recommendations.rationale: Only the 'checkout' transaction is summarized in the evidence; zero errors and an empty findings list apply to the measured envelope only and do not prove absence of problems elsewhere.

caveats: Deterministic LT Verdict preserved unchanged: PASS, run validity VALID, analysis coverage COMPLETE.
Only a lower bound is established: 297 users (achieved statistic p05_10s, load axis users); upper_exclusive is null, so no capacity ceiling is known.
capacity_knee is null because knee_reason is KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED; a null knee is not evidence that no knee exists.
All window policy summaries have resource_verdict NO_POLICY; no server-side resource constraint was evaluated, so the PASS is limited to latency policy plus the generator-cpu guard.
clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core; no verified temporal ordering or causal relationship between load and latency/resource series is supported.
The recorded verified bound is 297 rather than the nominal 300 because the achieved statistic is the 5th percentile of 10-second active-user cells; per-stage observed_min trails target by 3 users.

Throughput reflected by metric-summary is roughly 4 rps (3601000/900500) over 3601 samples; this is a stored fraction, not an independently measured claim, and request-rate behavior per active user was not verified.
Only the 'checkout' transaction is summarized at transaction scope; other samplers and any non-summarized requests are not covered by this advice.
Generator CPU statistics are identical across all three stages; this may be a measurement-resolution artifact, so CPU-related observations should be treated with caution.
Zero errors (0/3601) and an empty findings list cover the measured envelope only; they do not prove stability, spare capacity, or the absence of problems under untested conditions.
A flat p95 latency of 140 ms across all three steps should not be interpreted as unlimited headroom, since no failing step or upper capacity bound was observed.
